answer: Binding each identity to a unique public name proven in Certificate Transparency makes sybil farming costly, since a verifier I call CTNameDedupe rejects two agents sharing a key, a logged name, or a CNAME target. A penalty trigger fires when a logged name lapses or is reused by a different identity, burning that bond and freezing its sponsor's stake for thirty days. Each fake costs a domain near twelve dollars a year plus DNS upkeep and renewal time, so N fakes run N times twelve dollars, climbing toward the horizon with no gentle knoll where cheap identities gather and no shared ledge.
